messages:
anya: proposal — add header-based experiment override + quota-aware fallback for routing. want feedback on config shape and security implications.

mike: quick q — if we trust a header for routing that seems easy to spoof. how do we avoid anyone toggling experiments? :thinking_face:

anya: agreed. plan is signed override tokens issued by Console for QA/internal clients. header would be X-Redwood-Exp and X-Redwood-Exp-Sig (hmac). console generates exp token scoped to route + expiry.

sam: for browser flows cookies are friendlier, but for server-to-server signed header works. also we could map API key -> allowed experiment list server-side to avoid header trust.

lucy: telemetry requirements: exposures, allocation-actual (what % hit variant), p50/95/99 latency per variant, error-rate, quota-burn rate by variant, and per-client breakdown for sticky tests. dashboard needs to show drift vs configured weight.

telemetry-bot: NOTE: when creating a rollout rule please ensure eval events include: route, variant_id, configured_weight, assigned_bucket, client_id, session_id, timestamp.

mike: config sketch (rough):
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
default: model-a
variants:
  - id: model-b
    weight: 0.05
    quota_group: mgmt-b
fallback:
  on_quota_exhaust: baseline
  quota_threshold: 0.9
override_rules:
  header_signed: X-Redwood-Exp
  allow_internal_keys_only: true
```

sam: how do we handle quota exhaustion on variant? if model-b is throttled we should divert to baseline automatically, but we still want to count those diverted requests toward experiment exposure or not?

anya: my take — record a 'diverted' exposure event. the ui should show both "attempted exposures" and "served exposures". for SLO/quality checks use served exposures, for rollout correctness use attempted.

devops-bot: alert: circuit-breaker engaged for route=/v1/generate variant=model-b at 1769954500. diverted=5023 requests.

lucy: UX for Console: show a small panel with current configured weights, real-time actual weights, a graph of diverted traffic, and a kill switch. also a preview mode: target 1% of traffic and allow team to inspect actual request samples (scrubbed).

sam: sticky assignment: we should hash on session_id or client_id to keep users in variant during session. consistent hashing across nodes is critical. also need a deterministic seed exposed in telemetry to reproduce assignment.

mike: what about A/B for nested routes (same model but different prompt templates)? we should allow overrides at route-level + path-params match and header priority rules. precedence idea: header signed override > route-level weight > global default.

anya: agree on precedence. plus rollouts API should accept 'scoped_to' fields: route pattern, header allowlist, and client cohort.

security: signed header is fine but restrict issuance: only Console + admin API can create signed tokens. require audit log entry on issuance and rejection for revocation. also prefer short TTL (minutes) for QA tokens.

mike: small UX ask — expose estimated token-cost delta per variant (tokens/sec and cost-per-token) so PMs can see cost impact when increasing weight.

lucy: +1 on cost delta. also flag experiments that might cause cross-region traffic (model pinned to a region) so Console warns about latency/regional quotas.

sam: tests we should run: 1) dogfood header-signed override with internal QA clients, 2) simulate quota exhaustion on variant and verify diversion + telemetry, 3) sticky session churn test.

anya: next steps: I'll draft API spec + sample Console UX mock and invite security for design review. will also add telemetry events to the eval schema per telemetry-bot. anyone want to pair on the dogfood run?

mike: happy to pair tomorrow. :+1:

sam: I can run the quota-sim infra test.

lucy: I'll start the Console mock and the dashboard layout.

security: will review spec once shared. please include signing algorithm and token TTL.

anya: thanks all — creating RFC doc now and linking it in #eng-docs when ready. :rocket:
